title: Strategies to Identify Potential Radicalised Groups
what_it_is: Strategies to Identify Potential Radicalised Groups

sections.label: Radicalised Bangladeshis counter-terrorism efforts
sections.summary: Minister outlines follow-up efforts to identify radicalised groups, sharing intelligence with foreign partners and involving society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the recent discovery of radicalised Bangladeshis in Singapore, what are our follow-up efforts and strategies in identifying more of such activities or groups with high potential or likelihood of such ideologies within our midst.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: These threats can come from within Singapore or from foreigners in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As part of the overall counter-terrorism effort, we also share intelligence with foreign security partners to deal with the transnational nature of the threats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The larger Singaporean society has also got to play a part in protecting us against this threat.

sections.label: Foreign worker dormitory guidelines
sections.summary: Foreign worker dormitories are subject to guidelines on what is allowed and not allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Foreign worker dormitories are subject to a number of guidelines in terms of what we allow and do not allow.

sections.label: Security, foreign worker crime rates
sections.summary: Security is an ongoing conversation; crime incidence is lower among foreign workers than the general Singapore population.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The issue of overall security is an ongoing conversation, not just with people who manage foreign worker dormitories, but we need to involve the broader Singapore society and my Ministry will be announcing some plans soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you look at the incidence of crime, it is actually lower amongst the foreign workers because they are here for a purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If they get into trouble, they will be sent back straightaway and it is a huge economic cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the crime incidence within the foreign worker population is lower than that of the general Singapore population.

sections.label: Managing foreign worker population growth
sections.summary: The growth of the foreign worker population has been managed significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, we have to manage that and the growth of the foreign worker population has been managed significantly.
